description:
## Goal

Make large immutable product values shared across producers, ProductMemo, typed PullSession consumers, downstream products, World projections, direct pull results, and cache hits without changing product keys, semantic equality, generations, dependencies, or #110 behavior. Collapse the copied emission view and duplicate root-projection machinery so fewer concepts also perform less work.

## Combined-stack evidence

Authoritative parent: c5e1cd558a64f70211f5bc01dc54dfaa1de36c0c, PR #110 plus the first fourteen reviewed replays.

A temporary combined-stack 00420 probe measured 17,840 transfers of ProductValue variants that previously deep-cloned large payloads, 13,581 successful typed RuntimeDemand reads that previously cloned the inner demand, and 237 packaged-executable RuntimeDemand transfers. Sharing reduces this exact observed lower bound of 31,658 deep copies to zero. Surviving handoffs are Rc reference increments; the redundant producer-to-memo staging clone is deleted entirely. The lower bound excludes whole-program World/native handoffs and deletion of 237 EmissionReadyExecutable aggregate rebuilds.

The same drive contains 237 Materialized, 237 ABI, 237 Backend, and 237 packaged executable values plus 4,946 ABI callable-owner references. Permanent pointer proofs use a small fixture; the temporary 00420 counters and fixture substitution are removed.

The combined native corpus remains 510 candidates: 474 resolved, 2 known drive panics, 34 expected fatal paths, and 472 paired codegen successes. It preserves 5,763 semantic executable entries while physical sharing removes 55 roots, 146 continuations, 201 bodies, and 47,760 native bytes; MakeClosure remains 118. Work is 206 sharing passes, 18,569 indexed bodies, 17,769 owned graph bodies, 6,796 graph comparisons, and 6,107 body comparisons. Paired timing 12,796 -> 12,270 ms is corroborative, not a threshold.

## Combined model

Large immutable ProductValue payloads and BackendProgram / NativeProgram projections use Rc because PullSession and World are single-thread owned and do not cross a Send or Sync boundary. ABI retains Materialized and callable-construction owners; Backend retains ABI; packaged executables retain RuntimeDemand. Materialized local effects and transport remain distinct from ABI settled/transitive effects and completed transport.

Structural equality remains the movement rule. An equal recomputation preserves both generation and the prior canonical allocation. ProductMemo, ProductDriver return values, PullSession side inventories, Backend/Native root projections, World, macro consumers, and fresh product sessions all retain that canonical handle. Changed content advances generation and replaces it. Native equality remains exhaustive, including struct_schemas.

Recursive completion members share one validated Rc<ProductDependencies>. Demand settlement keeps one frozen Rc read view, uses a member-aligned Vec rather than a per-round HashMap of cloned executable keys for own-input overlays, and removes external handles before returning the member-only result.

EmissionReadyExecutable and EmissionReadyCallEdge are deleted; backend lowering reads the retained ABI/materialized model directly. NativeProgramMap and BackendProgramMap share RootProjectionMap rather than maintaining concordant slot implementations. PullSession parallel artifact maps remain transition state owned by fz-tfn.10, but their handles are canonical now.

## Acceptance and proof

1. Production large payload structs are non-Clone where practical; test-only Clone derives may build independent equality probes.
2. Rc::ptr_eq proves producer -> memo -> typed inventory -> Materialized -> ABI -> Backend -> packaged program -> World -> direct result -> cache hit, plus unchanged reproduction and a fresh product session.
3. Equal-but-distinct ProductMemo settlement, direct ProductDriver return, side-map recording, Backend/Macro/Native projection definition, and root packaging retain the prior canonical handle; changed values still move.
4. Structural generations, product keys, dependency capture, recursive-group validation, canonical artifacts, typed semantic ordering, backend request lifecycle, and runtime behavior remain unchanged.
5. Recursive group members retain one dependency snapshot; ordinary products retain their exact snapshot.
6. The temporary counters and large 00420 test substitution are removed. The permanent small ownership test adds negligible CI work; the ignored native measurement remains outside ordinary CI.
7. Focused ownership/generation/projection/demand/native/causal tests, fixture behavior, full library/integration tests, fmt, check, and strict clippy pass from one isolated target directory.

This is a representation and ownership collapse, not cache-key deduplication.
title: Share immutable product payloads instead of deep-cloning artifacts
